questions.question: Which statement best describes an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) in a VPC?
options: A logical component in a VPC that represents a virtual network card
A physical network adapter in the underlying host that is shared by all instances
A routing table that controls traffic between subnets in a VPC
A managed DNS record that maps a hostname to an instance's private IP
questions.explanation: The section defines an ENI as a logical component in a VPC that represents a virtual network card. A physical NIC shared by instances is not what an ENI is; route tables are separate VPC constructs, not ENIs; and DNS records are handled by Route 53, not by the ENI itself.

questions.question: A company is building a multi-tier application and wants one instance to present two distinct private IPv4 addresses to different internal components, while keeping a single network interface with a stable MAC address. What does the ENI configuration allow?
options: One primary private IPv4 plus one or more secondary private IPv4 addresses
Only a single private IPv4 address per ENI, with extras requiring a new ENI
Multiple primary private IPv4 addresses on the same ENI
Secondary private IPv4 addresses only when an Elastic IP is attached
questions.explanation: An ENI can have a primary private IPv4 address and one or more secondary IPv4 addresses. An ENI has exactly one primary address, so multiple primaries is wrong; extra addresses do not require a new ENI; and secondary addresses exist independently of Elastic IP attachment.

questions.question: An architect wants each private IPv4 address on a single ENI to be reachable from the internet, without relying on a public IPv4 address. Which statement matches the ENI capability described in the section?
options: You can associate one Elastic IP (IPv4) per private IPv4 address on the ENI
You can associate one Elastic IP per ENI, regardless of how many private IPv4 addresses it has
You can associate an Elastic IP only to the primary private IPv4 address of the ENI
You can associate multiple Elastic IPs to a single private IPv4 address
questions.explanation: The ENI attributes list one Elastic IP (IPv4) per private IPv4 address. Limiting Elastic IPs to one per ENI or to the primary address only contradicts that per-address mapping, and attaching multiple Elastic IPs to one private address is not the documented model.

questions.question: A VPC engineer needs the ENI to have a publicly routable address even though no Elastic IP will be allocated. According to the ENI attributes, which option satisfies this?
options: One public IPv4 address
One public IPv6 address
Two Elastic IP addresses
A secondary MAC address with public routing
questions.explanation: The listed ENI attributes include one public IPv4 address, which is separate from the Elastic IP option. Public IPv6 is not among the listed attributes, Elastic IP count per private IPv4 is one, and MAC addresses do not carry public routing.

questions.question: A security team wants traffic filtering for an instance's second network interface to differ from its first, and also wants to identify interfaces by their hardware address during auditing. Which combination of ENI attributes supports this?
options: One or more security groups and a MAC address
One Elastic IP and a route table
One public IPv4 address and a subnet CIDR block
A single security group shared by the whole VPC and a MAC address
questions.explanation: An ENI can have one or more security groups and has a MAC address, which lets filtering and identification be defined per interface. Elastic IPs and route tables are not listed as ENI attributes in this way, the public IPv4 is a separate attribute, and security groups are associated with resources such as ENIs, not with an entire VPC.

questions.question: A production EC2 instance in us-east-1a fails. The operations team needs to preserve its network configuration, including its private IP addresses and security groups, and attach it to a standby instance in the same AZ. What should the architect do?
options: Detach the ENI from the failed instance and attach it to the standby instance
Terminate the failed instance and let the standby instance inherit its ENI automatically
Create a new ENI in the standby instance's subnet and re-create the addresses manually
Move the standby instance into a different AZ so it can reuse the failed instance's ENI
questions.explanation: ENIs can be created independently and moved between EC2 instances on the fly for failover. ENIs are not inherited by other instances on termination, a newly created ENI would not preserve the existing interface and its configuration, and an ENI is bound to a single AZ so it cannot be attached to an instance in another AZ.
questions.keyTopic: Move ENI between instances for failover

questions.question: An application in availability zone us-east-1a must survive an AZ outage with minimal reconfiguration. A junior engineer proposes attaching the existing us-east-1a ENI to an instance launched in us-east-1b. Why does this plan fail?
options: An ENI is bound to a specific Availability Zone, so it can only be attached to instances in that same AZ
An ENI can be moved only after the Elastic IP is disassociated and then reassociated
An ENI can be attached only to the instance that originally created it
An ENI can be moved across AZs only through a VPC peering connection
questions.explanation: The ENI is bound to a specific Availability Zone, so it cannot follow an instance into another AZ. Elastic IP disassociation is not a prerequisite for AZ movement, ENIs are explicitly movable between instances, and VPC peering does not change an ENI's AZ binding.
questions.keyTopic: ENI bound to a single AZ

questions.question: Which two statements correctly describe how an ENI relates to an EC2 instance and its Availability Zone?
options: You can create an ENI independently and attach it to an instance on the fly, and the ENI stays within one AZ
You can create an ENI independently and attach it to instances in any AZ in the Region
An ENI cannot be moved between instances, but it can be moved between AZs
An ENI can exist only while it is attached to a running instance
questions.explanation: The section states ENIs can be created and attached to instances on the fly for failover and are bound to a specific AZ. Cross-AZ attachment contradicts that binding, moving between AZs is the opposite of the rule, and ENIs can exist independently of any instance.
questions.keyTopic: Move ENI between instances for failover

questions.question: A single EC2 instance needs a second network interface with its own private address and its own security group, rather than adding another address to the existing interface. What is the correct design?
options: Attach a secondary ENI (Eth1) to the instance in the same AZ
Add a secondary private IPv4 address to the existing primary ENI
Replace the primary ENI with a new interface to gain a second address
Attach the secondary ENI to the instance from a different AZ
questions.explanation: An instance can have a primary ENI (Eth0) and a secondary ENI (Eth1), each with its own address and security groups. Adding a secondary private IPv4 to the primary ENI does not create a separate interface; replacing the primary ENI does not add a second interface; and an ENI from another AZ cannot be attached because it is bound to its own AZ.
